findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State in the client-documentation story that registering the `evals` extra means adding an `evals` entry to `rebar._optional.EXTRAS` (probe module + blurb tuple, matching the existing shape) in addition to pyproject.toml:165, since AC3's `'evals' in EXTRAS` check reads `_optional.EXTRAS`, not pyproject.
evidence: pyproject.toml:165 `evals = ["genai-prices"]` registers the extra for pip
src/rebar/_optional.py:35-68 EXTRAS dict contains agents/tracing/grounding/grounding-terraform/metrics/wiki/adf/s3 — no `evals` key, so `'evals' in EXTRAS` is currently False
The two registries are independent: pyproject optional-dependencies drives pip resolution; _optional.EXTRAS drives the runtime guard_import/require_extra hint path
findings.finding: AC3's success check `from rebar._optional import EXTRAS; print('evals' in EXTRAS)` targets the rebar._optional.EXTRAS dict, but the `evals` extra is currently registered only in pyproject.toml [project.optional-dependencies] (line 165), not in _optional.EXTRAS (lines 35-68, which holds agents/tracing/grounding/.../s3). The plan's Context calls the extra 'unregistered' without stating that registration must add an entry to the _optional.EXTRAS dict (with a probe-module + blurb tuple matching the existing shape). As written, an implementer could add the pyproject entry alone — making `pip install nava-rebar[evals]` work — yet the AC3 assertion would still print False.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria, criterion 3 (`'evals' in EXTRAS` check); Context ("the `evals` extra is unregistered")
scenarios: Implementer registers the extra in pyproject only; make verify's AC3 assertion fails because EXTRAS lacks the key
An evals import later needs guard_import(extra='evals') but _optional.EXTRAS has no entry, so require_extra raises ValueError('unknown extra evals')
findings.suggested_fix: Add to criterion 3 / the documentation story: 'Register `evals` in `src/rebar/_optional.py` EXTRAS as `"evals": ("genai_prices", "<blurb>")` so `'evals' in EXTRAS` is True and `guard_import(..., extra="evals")` resolves; the pyproject.toml:165 entry already provides the pip dependency.'

findings.finding: Parent AC3's machine check is `rebar search 'status:open fixture-drift'` returning 0 rows, while child 741b closes/verifies via `rebar search "fixture-drift:" -o json | ... status=="open"` and selects tickets with `search("title:fixture-drift: status:open")`. The child scopes to the `title:fixture-drift:` prefix whereas the parent's query is an unqualified `fixture-drift` substring; if any open ticket matches the parent's broader query without a `title:fixture-drift:` prefix, the child's closure set misses it and the parent's 0-row check fails.
scenarios: An open ticket matches the parent's unqualified `fixture-drift` query via body/tag but lacks the `title:fixture-drift:` prefix; 741b's closure loop skips it and the parent's 0-row gate reports a non-zero count.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the identical query form the parent AC specifies for both selection and verification, or document that the two queries are provably equivalent on this corpus.
